title: Ampleness is invariant under isomorphisms of invertible modules
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and L and N invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] on X. If L and N are isomorphic as O_X-modules, then L is ample if and only if N is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Definition 01PS and Section 01PR; section-transport argument in Proposition 09NZ of varieties.tex, second sentence

proof.text: Tensor the given module isomorphism n times, with the identity of the structure sheaf in degree zero. This gives isomorphisms between every pair of tensor powers, compatible with restrictions and germs.

A linear isomorphism on stalks maps the maximal ideal times the entire stalk onto that same submodule on the target. Transport a section through the tensor-power isomorphism; its nonvanishing locus is unchanged.

The definition of ampleness is witnessed by compactness and, for each point, a positive tensor power, a section, and an affine open equal to its nonvanishing locus. Reuse the exponent and affine open for the transported section. The inverse isomorphism gives the reverse implication. The empty-space case has no points to check.
